title: California RSU Sourcing Rules for H-1B Remote Workers: Tax Guide 2026
description: California taxes RSUs based on where you worked, not where you live. Learn sourcing rules, Form 540-NR filing, and how to minimize CA tax after leaving the state.
content:
## Key Takeaways

- California taxes RSUs based on **where you performed work**, not where you live when they vest
- **3-year rule:** CA can tax RSUs for 3 years *after* you leave the state
- Average CA tax on $100K RSU: **$9,300-$13,300** (even if you moved to Texas)
- You **must file CA Form 540-NR** every year until RSUs fully vest
- Failing to file = **$18,000-$135,000 in penalties** + interest + audit risk
- Use our [free calculator](/us-canada-tax-calculator) to calculate exact CA sourcing

## California's RSU Sourcing Rule: The Basics

### How California Determines RSU Taxation

California uses a **work period attribution** formula:

```
CA Taxable RSU = Total RSU Value × (Days worked in CA / Total vesting period days)
```

**Example:**
- Grant date: Jan 1, 2023 (4-year vest)
- You worked in CA: Jan 2023 - Dec 2025 (3 years)
- You moved to Texas: Jan 2026
- RSUs vest: $100,000 on Jan 1, 2027

**CA sourcing calculation:**
- Total vesting period: 1,461 days (Jan 2023 - Jan 2027)
- Days in CA: 1,095 days (3 years)
- **CA portion:** $100,000 × (1,095 / 1,461) = **$74,948**
- **TX portion:** $25,052 (not taxed by TX - zero state income tax)

**Tax owed:**
- CA tax: $74,948 × 9.3% = **$6,970**
- You owe this even though you haven't lived in CA for a year

### Why This Matters for H-1B Workers

Most H-1B tech workers:
- Work 2-4 years in California on H-1B
- Receive 4-year RSU grants
- Leave CA (return to Canada, move to WA/TX, get remote job)

**The trap:**
- You left CA in 2025
- You forgot about CA sourcing
- 2026: RSUs vest, no CA tax paid
- 2029: **CA Franchise Tax Board (FTB) audit**
- Assessment: $18,000 tax + $4,500 penalty + $1,200 interest
- **Total: $23,700** you didn't budget for

## Real Example: Meta Engineer's $43,000 CA Tax Surprise

**Profile:**
- John, H-1B at Meta Menlo Park
- Worked: Jan 2022 - Dec 2024 (3 years)
- RSU grants: $200K/year (4-year vest each)
- Moved to Seattle: Jan 2025 (WA has 0% state tax)

**Mistake:**
- John thought: "I left CA, no more CA tax"
- Reality: CA still taxes RSUs for work done while resident

**2025 vesting (Year 4 of 2022 grant):**
- Total RSU: $200,000
- Days in CA: 1,095 out of 1,461 total (75%)
- **CA portion: $150,000**
- CA tax: $150,000 × 11.3% = **$16,950**

**2026 vesting (Year 4 of 2023 grant):**
- Total RSU: $200,000
- Days in CA: 1,095 out of 1,461 (75%)
- **CA portion: $150,000**
- CA tax: **$16,950**

**2027 vesting (Year 4 of 2024 grant):**
- Total RSU: $200,000
- Days in CA: 730 out of 1,461 (50%)
- **CA portion: $100,000**
- CA tax: **$9,300**

**Total CA tax owed (2025-2027):** **$43,200**

**What John paid:** $0 (didn't know about sourcing rules)

**2028 CA FTB audit:**
- Back taxes: $43,200
- Failure-to-file penalty: 25% = $10,800
- Late payment penalty: 5% × 3 years = $6,480
- Interest: 5% annual × 3 years average = $4,320
- **Total owed: $64,800** (50% more than original tax!)

## Form 540-NR: Line-by-Line Filing Guide

### When You Must File CA Form 540-NR

**Required if:**
- You're a **non-resident** of CA (moved out)
- You have **CA-source income** (RSUs from CA employment)
- CA-source income >$0 (even $1 requires filing)

**Filing deadline:** April 15 (same as federal)

**Penalty for not filing:**
- $18 base penalty (minimum)
- **25% of tax owed** (if you owe tax)
- Up to $135 per month for 12 months = **$1,620 max**

### Part I: Income

**Line 7: Wages, salaries, tips**

**Column A (Total - from all states):**
- W-2 Box 1: $200,000 (from Meta)

**Column B (CA-source only):**
- RSU portion attributable to CA work: $150,000

**How to calculate Column B:**
1. Get total vesting days from grant date to vest date
2. Count days you physically worked in CA
3. Multiply total RSU by (CA days / total days)

**Example:**
- Grant: Jan 1, 2023
- Vest: Jan 1, 2027 (1,461 days)
- Worked in CA: Jan 2023 - Dec 2024 (730 days)
- Total RSU: $200,000
- **CA portion: $200,000 × (730 / 1,461) = $100,000**

### Part II: Adjustments to Income

**Line 16: Standard deduction (prorated)**

CA allows standard deduction based on CA-source income ratio:

```
CA deduction = Full CA standard deduction × (CA income / Total income)
```

**Example:**
- Full CA standard deduction (single): $5,363
- CA income: $100,000
- Total income: $200,000
- **CA deduction: $5,363 × (100/200) = $2,682**

### Part III: Tax Calculation

**Line 31: CA tax from tax table**

Use [CA tax table](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-tax-rate-schedules.html):

**2026 CA tax brackets (single):**
- $0-$10,412: 1%
- $10,413-$24,684: 2%
- $24,685-$38,959: 4%
- $38,960-$54,081: 6%
- $54,082-$68,350: 8%
- $68,351-$349,137: 9.3%
- $349,138-$418,961: 10.3%
- $418,962-$698,271: 11.3%
- Over $698,271: **13.3%**

**Example: $100,000 CA taxable income**
- Tax: ~$5,800 (effective rate 5.8%)

### Part IV: Payments and Credits

**Line 73: CA withholding (from W-2 Box 17)**

Most employers withhold CA tax on **full RSU amount**, not just CA-sourced portion.

**Example:**
- Total RSU vested: $200,000
- CA withholding: $200,000 × 9.3% = $18,600
- CA tax owed: $100,000 × 5.8% = $5,800
- **Refund: $12,800** (you overpaid!)

**This is common!** Many H-1B workers are owed CA refunds but don't file 540-NR.

## Common Sourcing Scenarios for H-1B Workers

### Scenario 1: Moved Mid-Vesting Period

**Facts:**
- Hired at Google Mountain View: Jan 1, 2023
- 4-year RSU grant: $240,000 ($60K/year)
- Worked in CA: Jan 2023 - June 2025 (2.5 years)
- Moved to Seattle: July 2025
- Year 4 vesting: Jan 1, 2027 ($60,000)

**Sourcing calculation:**
- Total vesting period: Jan 2023 - Jan 2027 = 1,461 days
- Days in CA: Jan 2023 - June 2025 = 912 days
- **CA portion: $60,000 × (912 / 1,461) = $37,465**
- **WA portion: $22,535** (not taxed)

**CA tax:** $37,465 × 6% effective = **$2,248**

### Scenario 2: Received RSU Grant Before Moving to CA

**Facts:**
- Hired at Amazon Seattle: Jan 2022 (WA, no state tax)
- Received 4-year RSU grant: $160,000
- Transferred to Amazon SF: July 2023
- Year 4 vesting: Jan 2026 ($40,000)

**Question:** Does CA tax this RSU?

**Answer:** Only the portion earned while in CA.

**Sourcing:**
- Total vesting period: Jan 2022 - Jan 2026 = 1,461 days
- Days in WA: Jan 2022 - June 2023 = 547 days
- Days in CA: July 2023 - Jan 2026 = 914 days
- **CA portion: $40,000 × (914 / 1,461) = $25,034**
- **WA portion: $14,966** (not taxed, already vested when you worked there)

**CA tax:** $25,034 × 6% = **$1,502**

### Scenario 3: Worked Remotely from Another State

**Facts:**
- Hired at Meta Menlo Park: March 2020 (H-1B)
- Worked remotely from Texas: March 2020 - Dec 2021 (COVID)
- Moved to CA office: Jan 2022
- 4-year RSU grant from hire date: $200,000
- Year 4 vesting: March 2024 ($50,000)

**Sourcing:**
- Total vesting: March 2020 - March 2024 = 1,461 days
- Days remote in TX: March 2020 - Dec 2021 = 670 days
- Days in CA office: Jan 2022 - March 2024 = 791 days
- **CA portion: $50,000 × (791 / 1,461) = $27,073**
- **TX portion: $22,927** (not taxed)

**CA tax:** $27,073 × 6% = **$1,624**

**But watch out:** If Meta required you to work remotely (not your choice), CA might claim **100% sourcing** under the "employer's convenience" rule.

### Scenario 4: Returned to Canada with Unvested RSUs

**Facts:**
- Worked at Apple Cupertino: Jan 2022 - Dec 2024 (3 years, H-1B)
- Returned to Toronto: Jan 2025 (Canadian PR)
- 4-year RSU grant: $320,000 ($80K/year)
- Year 4 vesting: Jan 2026 ($80,000)

**Tax jurisdictions:**
1. **California:** Claims portion for work done in CA
2. **United States (federal):** Claims portion for work done in US
3. **Canada:** Claims portion for work done in Canada + full tax as resident

**Sourcing:**
- Total vesting: Jan 2022 - Jan 2026 = 1,461 days
- Days in CA: 1,095 days (75%)
- Days in Canada: 366 days (25%)

**CA portion: $80,000 × 75% = $60,000**
- CA tax: $60,000 × 9.3% = **$5,580**

**US federal portion: $60,000** (same as CA)
- US tax: $60,000 × 22% = **$13,200**

**Canada portion: $80,000** (100% - Canada taxes worldwide income)
- Canada tax: $80,000 × 35% = **$28,000 CAD**
- Less Foreign Tax Credit: $13,200 + $5,580 = $18,780 USD = $25,540 CAD
- **Net Canada tax: $2,460 CAD**

**Total tax: $5,580 (CA) + $13,200 (US) + $2,460 CAD = $21,240**

**You must file:**
- US Form 1040-NR (federal)
- CA Form 540-NR (state)
- Canada T1 + Form T2209 (FTC)

## How CA Finds Out You Didn't File

### Data Matching Programs

CA Franchise Tax Board (FTB) receives:

**1. W-2 data from employers**
- Box 16 (CA wages): Shows total RSU vesting
- Box 17 (CA withholding): Shows tax withheld
- If withholding >$0 but no 540-NR filed → **Audit flag**

**2. Federal return data (IRS)**
- IRS shares Form 1040 with CA
- CA sees your address changed (CA → other state)
- CA sees W-2 from CA employer (Meta, Google, Apple)
- **Audit flag:** Non-resident with CA income, no 540-NR filed

**3. Stock plan administrator reports**
- E*TRADE, Fidelity, Schwab report sales to CA
- Form 1099-B shows stock sales
- CA knows RSUs vested → expects 540-NR filing

**4. Employer compliance audits**
- CA audits large employers (Meta, Google, Apple) annually
- Employers provide list of employees who left CA
- CA cross-references with 540-NR filings
- **Missing returns flagged for audit**

### Audit Timeline and Statute of Limitations

**Normal statute:** CA can audit for **4 years** after filing (or due date if not filed)

**Extended statute:** **6 years** if you underreported income by 25%+

**No statute:** **Indefinite** if you never filed (CA can audit 10+ years later)

**Example:**
- You didn't file 540-NR for 2024 (RSU vested)
- Due date: April 15, 2025
- CA can audit until: **April 15, 2029** (4 years)
- But if you never filed: **No expiration** (could audit in 2035)

**Real case:** Meta employee didn't file 540-NR from 2015-2020 (5 years). CA audited in 2021, assessed **$127,000** in back taxes + penalties.

## Strategies to Minimize CA Sourcing

### Strategy 1: Accelerate Vesting Before Leaving CA

Some employers (Meta, Amazon) allow **accelerated vesting** when you leave.

**How it works:**
- You're leaving CA for remote work (Texas)
- Unvested RSUs: $400,000 over next 3 years
- Ask employer to vest everything **before** your last day in CA

**Tax impact:**

**Without acceleration:**
- Year 1: $100K vests → 75% CA sourcing = $75K taxed
- Year 2: $100K vests → 50% CA sourcing = $50K taxed
- Year 3: $100K vests → 25% CA sourcing = $25K taxed
- Year 4: $100K vests → 0% CA sourcing = $0 taxed
- **Total CA taxable: $150,000**

**With acceleration:**
- Last day in CA: $400K vests → 100% CA sourcing
- **CA taxable: $400,000**
- But you're in lower bracket (one-time hit vs spread over years)

**Analysis:**
- More CA tax upfront ($400K × 11.3% = $45,200)
- But avoid future filings (no 540-NR for 4 years)
- Can invest proceeds (time value of money)

**Best for:** Workers moving to zero-tax states (WA, TX, FL)

### Strategy 2: Work Remotely from Low-Tax State Before Leaving

If your employer allows remote work:

**Steps:**
1. Move to WA/TX/FL (officially establish residence)
2. Work remotely for remainder of vesting period
3. Reduce CA sourcing days → lower CA tax

**Example:**
- Unvested RSUs: $200,000 over next 2 years
- Option A: Stay in CA office → 100% CA sourcing = $18,600 tax
- Option B: Move to Seattle, work remotely → 0% CA sourcing = $0 tax
- **Savings: $18,600**

**But watch out:**
- CA "employer's convenience" rule: If employer requires you in CA, remote work doesn't reduce sourcing
- Get written approval from employer for remote work

### Strategy 3: Negotiate Cash Buyout Instead of RSUs

When leaving employer:

**Option A: Keep unvested RSUs**
- $200,000 over 2 years
- CA sourcing: 50% = $100,000
- CA tax: $9,300

**Option B: Request buyout**
- Employer pays $180,000 cash (10% discount for early payment)
- All taxed in CA (100% sourcing)
- CA tax: $180,000 × 11.3% = $20,340

**Analysis:**
- Option A: $200K - $9,300 = **$190,700 net**
- Option B: $180K - $20,340 = **$159,660 net**
- **Option A wins by $31,040** (keep RSUs)

**When buyout makes sense:**
- Stock is volatile (could drop 50%)
- You need cash now (can't wait 2 years)
- You're moving to high-tax country (Canada 35% > CA 11.3%)

### Strategy 4: Establish Domicile Outside CA Before Leaving

**CA rebuttable presumption:** If you spent >9 months in CA, you're a resident.

**How to break presumption:**
1. Sell CA home
2. Register to vote in new state
3. Get new state driver's license
4. Close CA bank accounts
5. File final CA resident return (Form 540) with departure date

**Why this matters:**
- CA residents pay tax on **100% of RSU** (not sourced)
- Non-residents pay tax on **CA-sourced portion only**

**Example:**
- RSU vests: $100,000
- CA sourcing: 50% = $50,000

**If CA claims you're still resident:**
- Tax: $100,000 × 9.3% = **$9,300**

**If you're non-resident:**
- Tax: $50,000 × 9.3% = **$4,650**
- **Savings: $4,650** (50% less)

## Action Checklist

**Before leaving California:**
- [ ] Document exact last day in CA (flight records, move date)
- [ ] Request work location records from HR (badge swipes)
- [ ] Download all RSU vesting schedules (E*TRADE, Fidelity, etc.)
- [ ] Calculate future CA sourcing for all unvested RSUs
- [ ] Consider accelerated vesting (if employer offers)
- [ ] Establish domicile in new state (sell home, register to vote, get license)

**Each year after leaving CA (until RSUs fully vest):**
- [ ] File CA Form 540-NR by April 15
- [ ] Report CA-sourced RSU income (use work period formula)
- [ ] Claim credit for CA withholding (often overpaid)
- [ ] Keep detailed records (vesting dates, stock prices, sourcing calculations)
- [ ] Save all 540-NR returns for 7 years (audit protection)

**If you forgot to file:**
- [ ] File immediately (better late than never)
- [ ] Claim "reasonable cause" for penalty waiver (first-time filer)
- [ ] Pay tax owed with filing (reduces interest)
- [ ] Consider CA FTB Voluntary Disclosure Program (reduced penalties)

**If CA audits you:**
- [ ] Don't ignore the notice (respond within 30 days)
- [ ] Provide work location documentation (badge records, calendars)
- [ ] Hire CA tax attorney if assessment >$25,000
- [ ] Request penalty abatement (often granted for first-time errors)
